summary: A single-page form on the login route (/login, or that route under the configured sub-path), submitted by a script handler. The fields carry test ids that the project publishes for its own end-to-end tests; releases before 10.2.3 carry the same texts as aria-label instead.

sources.title: Grafana 13.2.3 end-to-end selectors: the login url and the test ids of the username, password and submit controls, with the values used before 10.2.3
Grafana 13.2.3 password field: an input whose type starts as password and that carries the password test id
Grafana 13.2.3 UI input: the remaining props are spread on a native input
Grafana 13.2.3 UI button: a native button with the given type and the remaining props spread on it
Grafana 13.2.3 routes: the login page is /login
Grafana 13.2.3 login page: shows the login form, or a change-password form after a sign-in; its links are prefixed with the configured sub-url

Grafana 13.2.3 change-password form: reuses the password component, and with it the password test id, without a username field. profile/ChangePasswordForm.tsx and Signup/SignupPage.tsx at the same commit do the same.
Grafana 13.2.3 default configuration: root_url and serve_from_sub_path, the settings for serving Grafana under a sub-path

Grafana 9.5.21 end-to-end selectors: Username input field, Password input field, Login button

fixtures.note: The layout of 10.2.3 and later. Field ids are generated at run time and are left out.
The layout of releases before 10.2.3, on the same path. An alternative to fixture.html, not a later step.
The current layout as served from a sub-path; /grafana/ is an example prefix. The steps have no path gate, and this fixture shows that they match there.

staysInteractive.note: OAuth and SAML providers are buttons under the form. With the login form disabled by configuration only those remain.
After a sign-in the same page can show a change-password form (it has a skip button); nothing is typed there.

notes: No path gate, as agreed for applications whose every selector is application-specific: each alternative names a Grafana test id, or Grafana's older labels together with its current-password field, and the password and button alternatives require the login form's username field. Under a sub-path the route is that prefix followed by login. Current layout also read at 10.4.19, 11.6.0 and 12.4.0; older layout at 10.2.2 and 8.5.27 (tags read 2026-10-12). In 8.5.27 the button has no type attribute, so that release is not covered. The inputs are React-controlled and need real input events.
